answer: A reef of long-lived reputation works like this: every agent earns standing only through verified completed work over time, and standing decays if it goes idle. A bridge between two agent communities accepts a newcomer only if its home reef vouches with staked reputation that is slashed on fraud. Like a lantern carried into dark water, that stake makes each identity costly to fake and cheap to verify: an attacker must do real, slow, attestable work for every copy, while honest agents simply show their earned record.
